takeaways: AI infrastructure demand is driving massive capital intensity, with firms like CoreWeave and Nvidia-backed ventures facing significant debt and collateral risks as they scale to meet global compute needs.

Rising US Treasury yields and geopolitical energy shocks are tightening global financial conditions, pressuring emerging market valuations and forcing a strategic pivot toward domestic infrastructure and currency independence.

Structural inflation from climate-driven supply shocks and the rapid transition to BEVs in China are reshaping industrial strategies, as companies increasingly bypass public grids to secure mission-critical power.

items.title: China’s central bank eyes global yuan in first solo 5-year plan in over a decade
bullets: The PBOC’s 2026-2030 strategic plan prioritizes the internationalization of the renminbi and the expansion of the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) to reduce reliance on the US dollar-based financial infrastructure.

Beijing aims to transform into a 'financial powerhouse' by deepening two-way market access and enhancing the roles of Shanghai and Hong Kong as global financial hubs, signaling a long-term shift in capital flow strategies.
items.reason: Strategic shift in global reserve currency dynamics

items.title: Climateflation drives up food prices and living costs
bullets: Extreme weather events are now a primary driver of structural inflation, with research indicating that rising temperatures could increase annual global food inflation by up to 3.2% by 2035.

The impact of climate shocks is persistent, with heatwaves causing supply chain disruptions that influence consumer price indices for at least 12 months after the initial event, complicating central bank inflation targeting.
items.reason: Structural impact on long-term inflation trends

items.title: Exclusive-Sri Lanka central bank sees no need for further rate hikes this year, governor says
bullets: Governor Weerasinghe confirmed the central bank will maintain rates at 8.75% for the remainder of the year, citing that the full impact of the 100 basis-point May hike has yet to materialize in the economy.

Despite inflation reaching 7.3% due to energy supply disruptions from the regional conflict, the bank expects a return to its 5% target by early next year, prioritizing growth stability over further tightening.
items.reason: Monetary policy divergence in emerging markets

items.title: Supermicro tops Q4 earnings expectations, offers strong Q1 guidance, stock jumps
bullets: Supermicro reported Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.70, beating analyst expectations of $1.59, while revenue reached $11.1 billion, slightly missing the $11.2 billion consensus estimate.

The company provided a robust Q1 revenue forecast of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion, significantly exceeding the $11.9 billion expected by Wall Street, signaling continued momentum in its AI/IT solutions strategy.
items.reason: Strong earnings and guidance from a major AI infrastructure player.

items.title: CoreWeave stock pops 11% as revenue doubles on accelerating AI infrastructure demand
bullets: CoreWeave reported a 112% year-over-year revenue increase to $2.58 billion, supported by a massive $104 billion revenue backlog and 1.5 gigawatts of active power capacity.

Despite the growth, the company faces significant capital intensity, with projected 2026 capital expenditures reaching up to $39 billion and $35 billion in debt to fund its aggressive data center expansion.
items.reason: High-growth AI infrastructure provider with massive capital requirements.

items.title: Euro zone bond yields rise as oil climbs on Hormuz doubts
bullets: Euro zone yields are climbing as Brent crude prices surge toward $90 per barrel, driven by geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz that threaten to disrupt energy supplies.
Market participants have increased their expectations for European Central Bank tightening to 41 basis points for the remainder of the year, up from 37 basis points late last week.
items.reason: Geopolitical risk driving inflation expectations and ECB policy repricing.

items.title: US Treasury Yield Spike Puts South Korea’s Chip-Heavy Stock Market on Edge
bullets: The 30-year US Treasury yield has reached 5.28%, matching levels not seen since July 2007, creating significant pressure on global capital flows and emerging market valuations.

Rising US yields threaten to increase funding costs for major technology firms, potentially curbing capital expenditure in the semiconductor sector, which accounts for nearly half of the South Korean stock market.
items.reason: Significant move in long-end US Treasuries impacting global liquidity and equity risk premiums.

items.title: Wharf firms up balance sheet as Hong Kong sales cushion profit slump
bullets: Wharf Holdings reported a significant recovery in Hong Kong development revenue, which nearly tripled to HK$1.35 billion, helping to offset a 54% decline in mainland China property revenue.
The firm maintains a strong net cash position of HK$6.2 billion and is prioritizing reinvestment in Hong Kong property projects, signaling a strategic shift away from struggling mainland assets.
items.reason: Indicates a major developer's strategic pivot and capital allocation shift between HK and mainland markets.

items.title: Rich Hongkongers rank travel over real estate in shifting life goals: survey
bullets: A Standard Chartered survey of 1,058 affluent residents reveals that real estate has fallen to seventh place among life goals, with only 24% of respondents prioritizing home ownership.

Wealthy individuals are increasingly viewing travel as a form of 'intangible capital' and a primary investment for well-being, suggesting a long-term shift in consumption patterns for the city's high-net-worth demographic.
items.reason: Highlights a significant change in consumer sentiment and wealth allocation priorities among Hong Kong's affluent class.

items.title: Why Jensen Huang’s $500 billion AI financing plan faces a big risk from China
bullets: Nvidia has partnered with major asset managers including BlackRock and Blackstone to create a $500 billion financing pipeline, aiming to treat GPUs as long-term, revenue-generating infrastructure assets rather than depreciating hardware.

The model faces significant collateral risk if Chinese domestic compute capacity expands rapidly, potentially triggering a price war that would cause hardware values to plummet and undermine the asset-backed loan structure.
items.reason: Systemic financial risk to the AI infrastructure model.

items.title: Nebius Earnings Preview: Michael Burry Is Short but Prediction Markets See Nvidia, Meta Taking Center Stage
bullets: Nebius Group is reporting second-quarter earnings with revenue expectations of $573 million, representing a 400% year-over-year increase, while managing a massive $25 billion capital expenditure plan for 2026.

Investor Michael Burry has taken a direct short position in the stock, citing concerns over valuation, while market sentiment remains heavily tied to the company's $27 billion infrastructure deal with Meta and its deep integration with Nvidia's hardware.
items.reason: High-profile short interest and significant AI infrastructure exposure.

items.title: China sales numbers are in: EVs up while everything with an engine collapses
bullets: In July 2026, China's pure battery-electric vehicle (BEV) sales rose 6% year-over-year, while internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicle sales plummeted by 44%.
Despite a 3.9% decline in overall 'New Energy Vehicle' (NEV) sales—dragged down by weak PHEV and EREV performance—BEVs achieved a record 65.1% retail market share in China.
items.reason: Highlights a critical structural shift in the world's largest auto market.

items.title: VinFast's Expansion Mirrors the Global Shift in EV Growth
bullets: VinFast reported a 96% year-on-year increase in global EV deliveries for Q2 2026, totaling 70,085 units, with first-half deliveries reaching 128,662 vehicles.
The IEA notes that while EV growth is stagnating in China and the US, emerging markets like Vietnam, India, and Australia are seeing EV sales double, signaling a geographic shift in demand.
items.reason: Identifies the new growth engines for the EV sector amid saturation in traditional markets.

items.title: SpaceX Plans to Power $16.8B Terafab Without the Grid
bullets: SpaceX has secured a tax-abatement agreement to power its $16.8 billion Terafab semiconductor and AI campus in Texas entirely through onsite power plants and battery storage, bypassing the public electric grid.

This move represents a significant shift in industrial infrastructure strategy, as the facility will assume responsibility for critical power functions like voltage control and frequency regulation typically managed by utility providers.
items.reason: Signals a major shift toward self-sufficient, off-grid industrial power models.

items.title: Data center boom ushers in a new era of infrastructure risks and opportunities for insurers
bullets: Annual global investment in data centers is projected to double from $500 billion in 2024 to over $1 trillion by 2027, highlighting the massive scale of the current infrastructure build-out.

The global data center insurance market is expected to reach $24 billion by 2030, driven by the transition of data centers into mission-critical infrastructure with significant exposure to climate-related and operational risks.
items.reason: Quantifies the massive capital expenditure cycle and emerging insurance market opportunities.

items.title: Firefly Aerospace Announces Extension of Multi-Launch Agreement with Lockheed Martin Through 2031
bullets: Firefly Aerospace has secured a contract extension with Lockheed Martin to provide up to 25 launches through 2031, utilizing its upgraded Alpha Block II rocket configuration.

The partnership includes collaboration on sea-based launch solutions with Seagate Space, aiming to enhance national security capabilities through rapid, flexible access to space from diverse offshore platforms.
items.reason: Significant long-term contract win for a key private aerospace player.

items.title: H3 launches navigation satellite
bullets: Japan successfully deployed the Michibiki 7 navigation satellite via its H3 rocket, marking a critical recovery after a December launch failure that damaged previous hardware.

The Japanese government is targeting a significant increase in domestic launch frequency, aiming for 30 launches per year by the early 2030s to bolster national space infrastructure and competitiveness.
items.reason: Signals a recovery in Japanese launch capabilities and aggressive future capacity targets.
